identification.name: Nylon 12 (PA12)
identification.common_form_notes: The dominant SLS (Selective Laser Sintering) 3D printing powder — most SLS-printed nylon parts are PA12 unless otherwise specified. Also stocked as bulk rod/sheet for machining (extruded round bar up to 200mm dia., sheet/plate up to 50mm thick per Smiths Metal Centres), and used for its low moisture absorption and good chemical/fuel resistance in tubing and fittings.
identification.notes: Mechanical/thermal properties primarily from a Smiths Metal Centres extruded PA12 (polyamide 12, i.e. Nylon 12) manufacturer datasheet (natural/unfilled grade column; the same datasheet also lists a 30%-glass-filled grade, not stored here). This resolved several gaps and one prior uncertainty from the earlier AZoM-aggregate-sourced data: elongation at break is 200% per this datasheet — confirms the earlier decision to reject a different aggregate source's implausible ~1.9–2.1% figure as erroneous (PA12 genuinely is highly flexible). Melting point (178°C), Shore D hardness (78), and usable temperature range (−50 to +80°C long-term without high mechanical load; short-term max +140°C) were previously unavailable and are now populated with directly-applicable datasheet figures rather than left null. Yield strength updated to this datasheet's directly-labeled "Tensile strength @ yield" (50 MPa), superseding an earlier derivation from a different source's ambiguously-named "Elastic Limit" row. Thermal conductivity (0.30 W/m·K) and CTE (coefficient of thermal expansion) (100 µm/m·K, average 20–60°C) also updated to this single dedicated datasheet's values, preferred over a generic aggregate database's range. Tensile strength (ultimate, 55 MPa) and compressive strength (49 MPa) retained from the earlier AZoM source, since this datasheet reports only a yield figure, not distinct ultimate-tensile or compressive values. Glass transition (56.85°C, from AZoM) and melting point (178°C, from this datasheet) are both populated, reflecting PA12's real semi-crystalline behaviour — it has both a melting point (Tm) and a glass transition (Tg), unlike purely crystalline or purely amorphous materials, which typically show only one or the other.

typical_usage: SLS-printed functional prototypes and end-use parts (brackets, housings, snap-fits, living hinges) needing good impact toughness and low moisture pickup; bearing and gearbox components; sealing/dampening elements valued for noise and vibration damping; fuel lines, pneumatic tubing, and quick-disconnect couplings where chemical resistance matters. Choose over PA6 when moisture stability, impact toughness, or SLS printability is the priority; choose PA6 (or POM) instead for higher stiffness/strength bulk-machined parts.
